title: Decision of the AI Office
summary: The AI Office has issued a decision regarding its policies on AI use and governance. It outlines guidelines and responsibilities for stakeholders to ensure responsible and compliant deployment of AI systems.

title: AI Office Vacancy: Technology Specialists in AI
summary: The document announces a vacancy for a technology specialist in an AI office. It outlines the responsibilities and qualifications needed, emphasizing expertise in AI development, data analysis, and related technologies.

title: AI Office Vacancy: Lead Scientific Adviser
summary: The document announces an open position for a Lead Scientific Adviser within the AI Office. It outlines the role’s responsibilities, qualifications, and the application process for candidates interested in guiding AI research and policy at a high level.

title: AI Office Vacancy: Legal Officers
summary: This policy announces a vacancy for Legal Officers in the AI Office, detailing the roles, responsibilities, and qualifications required for the position. Interested candidates are encouraged to review the eligibility criteria and apply through the designated submission process.

title: AI Office Vacancy: Policy Officers
summary: The document outlines the roles and responsibilities for policy officers in an AI office. It explains how vacancies will be filled, ensuring that qualified professionals guide AI policy and governance.

title: AI Act Scientific Panel
summary: The AI Act Scientific Panel is a group of experts who study the impact of the EU’s AI legislation and offer advice on how it should be applied and improved. They evaluate technical, ethical, and societal aspects of AI systems to help policymakers make informed decisions.

title: Draft Standardisation Request
summary: The document is a draft request asking for standardisation of certain AI-related processes or criteria. It proposes guidelines and a framework that could be used to ensure consistency and quality across AI products and services.

title: CoP Consultation Notice
summary: The document is a notice announcing a consultation process about establishing or developing a Community of Practice. It invites stakeholders to provide input and participate in shaping the initiative.

title: CoP Call for Expression of Interest
summary: This document invites individuals or organizations to express their interest in joining a Community of Practice (CoP). It outlines the purpose, scope, and expected contributions of the CoP and provides a form for submitting expressions of interest.

title: CoP Graphic: Overview of Iterative Drafting Process
summary: The document explains how a community of practice develops and refines its policies or guidelines through repeated drafts and feedback. It outlines a step‑by‑step, collaborative process that encourages continuous improvement and consensus before finalizing any official documentation.

title: CoP Graphic: Timeline of Drafting Process
summary: This document presents a visual timeline detailing the drafting process for the Community of Practice (CoP) policy, outlining key milestones, stakeholder contributions, and decision points. It serves as a reference to help stakeholders understand how the policy evolved over time and the steps involved in its development.

title: Code of Practice: 1st Draft
summary: This document sets out an initial set of guidelines for the responsible use of artificial intelligence, aiming to help developers, users, and regulators understand key ethical and safety expectations. It is a first‑draft framework that invites feedback and collaboration from stakeholders before a final version is adopted.

title: Code of Practice: 2nd Draft
summary: The Code of Practice: 2nd Draft offers detailed guidelines for the responsible design, deployment, and use of AI systems, focusing on safety, transparency, and privacy. It establishes standardized best practices that organizations should follow to meet regulatory and ethical requirements.

title: Code of Practice: 3rd Draft
summary: This document presents the third draft of a Code of Practice for AI, offering detailed guidelines on responsible development, deployment, and use of artificial intelligence. Its goal is to help organisations ensure ethical, safe, and compliant AI practices by promoting transparency, accountability, and adherence to relevant laws.

title: AI Pact Draft
summary: The AI Pact Draft is a proposed agreement that aims to guide how artificial intelligence is developed, deployed, and used, focusing on responsible, safe, and ethical practices. It calls for cooperation among stakeholders to promote transparency, accountability, and collaboration in AI technology.

title: AI Pact Final
summary: The AI Pact Final outlines a comprehensive framework for responsible AI development, emphasizing transparency, accountability, and collaboration among stakeholders. It establishes shared principles, regulatory guidelines, and mechanisms to ensure AI technologies are safe, ethical, and beneficial to society.

title: Guidelines on prohibited artificial intelligence (AI) practices
summary: This policy details AI practices that are prohibited, covering activities like creating disinformation, manipulating opinions, and exploiting vulnerable populations. It urges organizations to avoid these behaviors and implement safeguards for responsible AI deployment.

title: Guidelines on AI System Definition
summary: This policy outlines the criteria for defining what constitutes an AI system, specifying the technical and functional characteristics that must be present. It offers guidance on classifying such systems and explains how they are governed under the broader AI regulatory framework.

title: Communication on Boosting Start-Ups & Innovation
summary: This policy outlines how to effectively communicate initiatives aimed at boosting start-ups and driving innovation across the economy. It emphasizes clear messaging, stakeholder engagement, and transparent metrics to ensure support programs are understood and widely adopted.

title: EuroHPC Initiative for Start-Ups
summary: The EuroHPC Initiative for Start-Ups is a European program that offers high‑performance computing resources and support to early‑stage companies, helping them develop and deploy advanced computing solutions. It provides access to cutting‑edge HPC infrastructure, expertise, and funding opportunities to accelerate innovation and competitiveness in the European tech ecosystem.

title: Slideshow: Webinar on Risk Management
summary: This webinar focuses on risk management in AI, explaining how to identify, assess, and mitigate potential risks. Participants learn practical strategies and best practices to ensure responsible AI deployment.

title: Video: Webinar on Risk Management
summary: This webinar explores how organizations can identify, assess, and mitigate risks in the use of AI technologies. It covers best practices, regulatory considerations, and strategies to embed risk management into AI development and deployment.
